entities.summary: Yonatan "Yoni" Netanyahu was an Israeli military officer who commanded Sayeret Matkal during the Entebbe raid. The raid was launched in response to the 1976 hijacking of an international civilian passenger flight from Israel to France by Palestinian and German militants, who took control of the aircraft during a stopover in Greece and diverted it to Libya and then to Uganda, where they received support from Ugandan dictator Idi Amin. Though Israel's counter-terrorist operation was a success, with 102 of the 106 hostages being rescued, Netanyahu was killed in action – the only Israeli soldier killed during the crisis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Yonatan Netanyahu's leadership during the Entebbe raid had significant regional impact, demonstrating Israel's ability to counter terrorist threats and influencing the country's approach to counter-terrorism. His actions also led to increased international scrutiny of Palestinian militant groups.
